## Overview

This hands-on exercise focuses on visualising distribution using ridgeline plots and raincloud plots.

## Setup


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
if (!require(pacman)) install.packages("pacman")

pacman::p_load(
  ggdist,
  ggridges,
  ggthemes,
  colorspace,
  tidyverse
)

exam <- read_csv("Exam_data.csv")
```
:::

# 1. Visualising Distribution with Ridgeline Plot

## 1.1 Basic Ridgeline Plot


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(
  exam,
  aes(
    x = ENGLISH,
    y = CLASS
  )
) +
  geom_density_ridges(
    scale = 3,
    rel_min_height = 0.01,
    bandwidth = 3.4,
    fill = colorspace::lighten("#7097BB", 0.3),
    color = "white"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "English grades",
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    name = NULL,
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.2, 2.6))
  ) +
  theme_ridges()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](hands_on_exercise_4a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


## 1.2 Ridgeline Plot with Gradient Fill


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(
  exam,
  aes(
    x = ENGLISH,
    y = CLASS,
    fill = after_stat(x)
  )
) +
  geom_density_ridges_gradient(
    scale = 3,
    rel_min_height = 0.01
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    name = "English score",
    option = "C"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "English grades",
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    name = NULL,
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.2, 2.6))
  ) +
  theme_ridges()
```

```

```

## 1.3 Ridgeline Plot with Tail Probability


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(
  exam,
  aes(
    x = ENGLISH,
    y = CLASS,
    fill = 0.5 - abs(0.5 - after_stat(ecdf))
  )
) +
  stat_density_ridges(
    geom = "density_ridges_gradient",
    calc_ecdf = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(
    name = "Tail probability",
    direction = -1
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "English grades",
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    name = NULL,
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.2, 2.6))
  ) +
  theme_ridges()
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stderr}

```
Picking joint bandwidth of 3.18
```

## 1.4 Ridgeline Plot with Quartile Lines


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(
  exam,
  aes(
    x = ENGLISH,
    y = CLASS,
    fill = factor(after_stat(quantile))
  )
) +
  stat_density_ridges(
    geom = "density_ridges_gradient",
    calc_ecdf = TRUE,
    quantiles = 4,
    quantile_lines = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(name = "Quartiles") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "English grades",
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    name = NULL,
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.2, 2.6))
  ) +
  theme_ridges()
```

## 1.5 Ridgeline Plot with 95% Probability Range


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(
  exam,
  aes(
    x = ENGLISH,
    y = CLASS,
    fill = factor(after_stat(quantile))
  )
) +
  stat_density_ridges(
    geom = "density_ridges_gradient",
    calc_ecdf = TRUE,
    quantiles = c(0.025, 0.975)
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    name = "Probability",
    values = c("#FF0000A0", "#A0A0A0A0", "#0000FFA0"),
    labels = c("(0, 0.025]", "(0.025, 0.975]", "(0.975, 1]")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "English grades",
    expand = c(0, 0)
  ) +
  scale_y_discrete(
    name = NULL,
    expand = expansion(add = c(0.2, 2.6))
  ) +
  theme_ridges()
```

# 2. Visualising Distribution with Raincloud Plot

## 2.1 Half-eye Plot


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(
  exam,
  aes(
    x = RACE,
    y = ENGLISH
  )
) +
  stat_halfeye(
    adjust = 0.5,
    justification = -0.2,
    .width = 0,
    point_colour = NA
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Half-eye Plot of English Scores by Race",
    x = "Race",
    y = "English score"
  )
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](hands_on_exercise_4a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-8-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


## 2.2 Half-eye Plot with Boxplot


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(
  exam,
  aes(
    x = RACE,
    y = ENGLISH
  )
) +
  stat_halfeye(
    adjust = 0.5,
    justification = -0.2,
    .width = 0,
    point_colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.20,
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "English Scores by Race",
    x = "Race",
    y = "English score"
  )
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](hands_on_exercise_4a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-9-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


## 2.3 Half-eye Plot with Boxplot and Dot Plot


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(
  exam,
  aes(
    x = RACE,
    y = ENGLISH
  )
) +
  stat_halfeye(
    adjust = 0.5,
    justification = -0.2,
    .width = 0,
    point_colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.20,
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  stat_dots(
    side = "left",
    justification = 1.2,
    binwidth = 0.5,
    dotsize = 2
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Raincloud-style Distribution of English Scores",
    x = "Race",
    y = "English score"
  )
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](hands_on_exercise_4a_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-10-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::


## 2.4 Final Raincloud Plot


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(
  exam,
  aes(
    x = RACE,
    y = ENGLISH
  )
) +
  stat_halfeye(
    adjust = 0.5,
    justification = -0.2,
    .width = 0,
    point_colour = NA
  ) +
  geom_boxplot(
    width = 0.20,
    outlier.shape = NA
  ) +
  stat_dots(
    side = "left",
    justification = 1.2,
    binwidth = 0.5,
    dotsize = 1.5
  ) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_economist() +
  labs(
    title = "Raincloud Plot of English Scores by Race",
    x = "Race",
    y = "English score"
  )
```

## Learning Reflection

In this exercise, I learned that ridgeline plots are useful for comparing score distributions across many groups, while raincloud plots combine density, boxplot, and raw observation views into one chart.
